year
label: Year
description: The year the planets are set to, 1800 to 2050 (the span of JPL's elements the positions come from). Drag it to run the orrery through the years: every arm turns by its gears.

name: day_of_year
label: Day of the year
description: 1 is 1 January, 32 is 1 February, 60 is 1 March (61 in a leap year), 182 is 1 July (183), 305 is 1 November (306), at noon; 366 only in a leap year. One turn of the crank is one sidereal year: drag this to turn it.

name: set_year
label: Arms set in
description: The year you set the arms: at noon on 1 January of it every bead stands at its body's real mean longitude, and from then on the gears drive them, drifting by each train's error. Set it to the year you finish the orrery.

name: planet_set
label: Planets
description: The planets round the Sun, from Mercury out to the Earth, Mars, Jupiter or Saturn, the planets known before 1781. Each has its own two-stage gear train and tube.

name: moon
label: Moon
description: The Moon round the Earth: its own train to a tube, and under the Earth's arm a wheel, three idlers and a second wheel that keep the tube's turn (parallel motion), so it goes round once a sidereal month.

name: period_error
label: Largest period error (%)
description: How far any train's period may be from the real sidereal period, in percent. The smallest gearbox that meets it is chosen from the searched trains; a tighter value needs more teeth. The least value is the best the search found for these planets with at most 104 teeth (0.06 % with all and the Moon).

name: gear_module
label: Module
description: Tooth size: a gear's pitch diameter is the module times its teeth. The whole gearbox grows with it. At least 1.5 mm, so that the narrowest tooth space is as wide as the 1 mm brass sheet is thick; at most what keeps the largest gear within 160 sheet thicknesses (160 mm), so it stays flat (2.5 mm only for small trains).

name: laser_kerf
label: Laser kerf
description: The width your laser cuts away, for the cut file (cut.export moves each cut half of it off the part). 0 when your cutting service compensates it itself.

name: orrery_diameter
label: Span of the orbits
description: The circle the outermost bead sweeps. Each orbit is the one inside it plus what both beads need, and the rest is shared out evenly (not to scale). Its least keeps neighbouring beads apart at every date and takes the outermost bead round outside the plinth; its most keeps the outermost arm (one 36 in rod) and the Earth's carrier drooping less than 3 mm.

name: bead_set
label: Beads
description: Wooden beads for the Sun and planets, painted: small (Sun 30 mm), medium (40 mm) or large (50 mm). In the order of the real sizes, not to scale.

title: Geared orrery
description: A hand-cranked brass orrery: the Sun, Mercury to Saturn and the Moon, each on its own tube, driven from one crank through two gear stages whose tooth counts were searched so that every period is within the error you choose of the real sidereal period. Set the date and every bead stands where its gears put it, at its real mean longitude. Involute gears (ISO 53 rack, 20 degrees) laser cut from 1 mm brass, K&S telescopic brass tubes, 1/8 in brass rod, painted wooden beads, a walnut plinth. Export: cut.export {"path": "orrery.dxf", "kerf": "laser_kerf / 2", "copies": true, "width": "600 mm"} (width: your laser's bed) writes every brass part to cut, each once on its own layer (or File > Export > Sheet of set: Laser cut sheet, without kerf). The outputs give the tube and rod lengths to cut, where to drill the plinth, and where to set each arm on the degree ring.
